claims.head: A shadow job for Girgensons, Holmberg and Mikheyev
claims.call: The Lightning’s L3 (Girgensons, Holmberg and Mikheyev) spends at least 69% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canucks’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Mikheyev’s line (Girgensons, Holmberg and Mikheyev) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canucks’ first line is DeBrusk, Pettersson (#40) and Lekkerimäki.
claims.nums: At home: 69% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 34% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Jon Cooper likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canucks’ first line.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 46%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Max Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, up from 4% last season.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 6 of their last 7 games, including the last one. Nikita Kucherov takes shifts on two lines, L1 and L2. Emil Lilleberg is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Hedman and McDonagh.
Yanni Gourde is on the injured non-roster list (hip surgery) and has not played this season. Ilya Mikheyev has taken his spot beside Zemgus Girgensons and Pontus Holmberg.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 41% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 28 seconds at a time, against 67 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (9 of 16 changes).

TBL.head: The Lightning should be in control
TBL.body: Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. If the Canucks want to spoil it, start with getting good looks.

VAN.head: A steep climb for the Canucks
VAN.body: Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Canucks can still win it if they get good looks, but a lot has to go their way.
